{
  "role": "Analyst",
  "assumptions": [
    "nu > 0 fixed; incompressible unforced 3D Navier-Stokes on R^3.",
    "Initial velocity u0 is smooth, divergence-free, and rapidly decaying (e.g., Schwarz class).",
    "Solution is assumed to evolve in a suitable function class on [0,T); global regularity means extendability to all T>0.",
    "Any claimed a priori bound must be derived from the equations and admissible initial data, not imported from an unproved regularity criterion.",
    "Review must distinguish local existence, blow-up criteria, and global extension arguments.",
    "Invariance under scaling and Galilean symmetry should be tracked where relevant."
  ],
  "obligations": [
    "Obligation 1 — Provide a genuine a priori bound sufficient to prevent finite-time blow-up, e.g., a uniform-in-time critical norm bound such as ||u(t)||_{L^3(R^3)} or ||u(t)||_{H^{1/2}} on every finite interval; any such claim must be marked unverified unless fully proved.",
    "Obligation 2 — Show that the assumed function class and energy estimates allow continuation past any possible singular time, by excluding concentration or establishing a continuation criterion with controlled norms; this must be checked under the same assumptions."
  ],
  "failure_modes": [
    "Assuming a critical norm is bounded without proof.",
    "Using a regularity criterion that itself requires more regularity than assumed.",
    "Confusing local existence with global existence.",
    "Ignoring scaling-critical quantities or treating subcritical bounds as sufficient.",
    "Relying on properties of the initial data that are not preserved in the proof."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "This is an exploratory review structure only, not a proof or disproof; no claim of global regularity is established.",
    "All mathematical claims above are unverified unless directly stated as assumptions.",
    "Does not address specific known partial results or reductions."
  ]
}

{
  "role": "Independent Auditor",
  "assumptions": [
    "Setting: unforced incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes on R^3, viscosity nu > 0, smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free initial velocity.",
    "Scope: review checklist for an energy estimate and a continuation criterion; not a solution to global regularity.",
    "Audience expects separation of exact identities from inequalities/estimates."
  ],
  "obligations": [
    "Verify before use: equations written in the stated setting, with domain R^3 and divergence-free initial data.",
    "Energy identity checklist: confirm it is an identity, not an estimate. Check it follows from the equations by multiplying by u, integrating over R^3, and integrating by parts. Verify boundary/decay terms at infinity vanish; verify the nonlinear term integrates to zero using incompressibility and decay; verify the viscous term sign and constants; verify no hidden local-in-time or finite-domain assumption.",
    "Energy estimate checklist: confirm it is an inequality, not an identity. Check hypotheses used (regularity, decay, divergence-free, time interval, possible cutoff/truncation). Check whether constants depend on u0, nu, T, or unknown quantities. Check if the estimate is conditional or a priori; do not infer global control from a local estimate without a continuation argument.",
    "Continuation criterion checklist: verify the criterion is stated for a local smooth solution on [0,T), with precise norm and blow-up condition. Check equivalences among norms only if proved under stated regularity. Check whether the criterion is necessary, sufficient, or both; do not assume a bound alone proves existence beyond T without a separate local-existence/restart step. Mark all mathematical claims unverified unless directly established in this response."
  ],
  "failure_modes": [
    "Treating an energy identity as if it already implies an estimate.",
    "Treating an energy estimate as if it already implies global regularity.",
    "Using integration by parts without justifying decay/boundary terms at infinity.",
    "Assuming the nonlinear term vanishes in the energy identity without checking divergence-free and decay hypotheses.",
    "Confusing a continuation criterion with a global existence proof.",
    "Using norm equivalence without the regularity needed to justify it.",
    "Allowing constants to depend on unproved or unknown quantities.",
    "Applying finite-domain estimates to R^3 without checking boundary terms."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "This checklist does not solve or claim progress on global regularity for 3D Navier-Stokes.",
    "Mathematical claims here are unverified unless directly established in this response.",
    "No citations are provided or implied.",
    "Review structure only; no original proof, counterexample, or numerical evidence is supplied.",
    "Does not address forced, bounded-domain, periodic, or non-decaying data unless separately specified."
  ]
}

{
  "role": "Synthesis Chief",
  "assumptions": [
    "The candidate addresses only the stated unforced incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes Cauchy problem on R^3 with nu>0 and smooth, rapidly decaying, divergence-free initial data.",
    "The review is exploratory: the goal is to organize evidence and objections, not to declare a solution or establish consensus.",
    "Any mathematical assertion not directly established in this response is marked unverified."
  ],
  "obligations": [
    "Create exactly five checklist items that a future group-generated candidate must satisfy before any seriousness assessment.",
    "Each checklist item must state required evidence, the reviewer who could supply it, and one unresolved objection that must be preserved.",
    "Do not vote, do not claim consensus, and do not present the checklist as a proof or a resolution."
  ],
  "failure_modes": [
    "Allowing a checklist item to presuppose that the candidate is valid.",
    "Losing unresolved objections by summarizing them as mere caveats rather than preserving them as live review blockers.",
    "Treating the checklist as a decision procedure rather than an evidence-organizing tool.",
    "Accepting evidence from one role as if it already existed or had been independently reproduced."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "This checklist does not establish global smoothness for the 3D Navier-Stokes equations.",
    "All mathematical claims about the candidate are unverified unless a future review directly establishes them.",
    "The checklist is review-structure only: it cannot confirm existence, regularity, uniqueness, or blow-up criteria.",
    "No citations or external results are asserted or relied upon here."
  ]
}
